skill.name: brewpage-publish-safe
skill.description: Publish approved pages, files, and static sites to BrewPage. Store anonymous ownership locally and update the exact saved publication.
skill.summary: Publish to BrewPage and retain workspace ownership for in-place updates.
skill.author: kochetkov-ma

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are documentation, validation, or fixed local operations. Confirmed exposure includes first-party transfers, reusable plaintext owner proof, and executable lookup through unverified PATH directories. Review also found incomplete ZIP metadata checks and implicit owner reuse; no evidence of author prompt injection or undisclosed external destinations was found.

remediation.issue: ZIP review does not cover all bytes sent to BrewPage.
remediation.suggestion: Rebuild supplied archives from reviewed regular members without comments or extra metadata. Require approval of the final manifest and digest before uploading the rebuilt archive.

remediation.issue: Archive, Git, and upload tools depend on unverified executable lookup.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve each tool from a trusted absolute toolchain. Validate directory, executable, and symlink target ownership and write permissions before placing tools on PATH.

remediation.issue: A new create can attach existing owner authority without an explicit selection.
remediation.suggestion: Default new publications to fresh anonymous ownership. Require an exact saved target and explicit consent before reusing the existing token.

remediation.issue: Reusable owner proof and password headers are retained as plaintext.
remediation.suggestion: Store long-lived owner proof in the OS credential store. Deliver short-lived request headers through a private stream where practical and preserve restrictive state permissions.

remediation.issue: Ordinary file snapshots may exceed review limits before copying stops.
remediation.suggestion: Apply the input size limit before opening the output and enforce the same bound while copying. Remove partial output on failure.

remediation.issue: Local recovery records cannot independently prove a remote create outcome.
remediation.suggestion: Use server-supported idempotency and operation lookup if available. Otherwise retain pending state until documented service behavior or independent first-party evidence establishes the outcome.

semantic_findings.title: Unreviewed ZIP metadata is transmitted
semantic_findings.description: The secret check reads member names and file contents, not all ZIP metadata. The runner uploads supplied archives without removing unreviewed comments and extra fields.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parser accepts comments and does not inspect arbitrary extra-field values for secrets. The multipart upload sends the complete archive.

semantic_findings.title: New publications can silently reuse existing ownership
semantic_findings.description: A create without an owner target can select the sole saved workspace token. The publish instructions do not require affirmative approval for that authority reuse.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Selection considers all retained rows when the target is empty. One distinct saved token is written to the request header unless anonymous mode was chosen.

semantic_findings.title: Create recovery is not tied to a server operation identifier
semantic_findings.description: The request fingerprint is local, and reconciliation trusts an operator attestation. Most HTTP client errors also clear pending state without a verified no-write outcome.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local fingerprint is recorded before dispatch, but no server idempotency key is sent. Incorrect reconciliation or ambiguous rejection could permit an unintended duplicate.

content.user_title: Publish and Update Content on BrewPage
content.value_statement: Publishing a file or site also means tracking who can update it. BrewPage Publish Safe sends approved content and keeps ownership records for later updates.
actual_capabilities: Publish approved HTML, Markdown, JSON, individual files, or static sites to the BrewPage REST API.
Build a ZIP from a selected site directory or inspect a supplied ZIP. Return a manifest and require digest approval for flagged archives.
Check selected inputs for common credential formats, exclude known private paths, and reject opaque nested archives.
Set an expiration at creation and optionally select password protection from an owner-only file.
Retain anonymous owner proof in private per-workspace state and use it to update the exact saved publication.
Report pending creates and recover saved ownership or record an independently verified outcome.
limitations: Requires Bash, Python 3.8 or newer, Node.js, curl, and jq on macOS or Linux. ZIP workflows also need zip and unzip.
Credential checks are limited to recognizable patterns. They do not cover every encoded secret or all ZIP metadata.
This edition does not provide connected account ownership, private receipt delivery, or custom reader domain management.
Updates require saved owner proof in the original workspace and preserve the current visibility, password, and expiration.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a local file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Check a source without uploading it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Probe the selected draft locally and report its file type and size. Do not contact BrewPage or publish anything.

prompt_templates.title: Publish a reviewed draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Publish the reviewed Markdown draft to BrewPage under the specified non-public namespace for seven days. Use fresh anonymous ownership and no password.

prompt_templates.title: Update the same reader link
prompt_templates.prompt: In the original workspace, update the exact saved reader link with my approved replacement. Keep the existing access settings and expiration. Do not create another publication.

prompt_templates.title: Review a static site release
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review an archive before approving a write.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the dedicated site build and its entry file without uploading. Check all selected content and archive metadata. Ask me to approve the final archive before uploading.

output_examples.input: Publish an approved Markdown draft without public listing.
output: Publication confirmed. The BrewPage reader link is ready to share.
Anonymous owner proof was saved in private workspace state.

output_examples.input: Publish a site ZIP with entries requiring approval.
output: No upload was made. The archive manifest lists the files, selected entry, and flagged names.
Approve the exact archive digest before continuing.

output_examples.input: Update a reader link without matching owner proof.
output: The target could not be matched to saved owner proof. No update or new publication was sent.

best_practices: Review the exact files, page state, and archive metadata before authorizing an external write.
Choose fresh anonymous ownership or expressly approve reuse. Keep owner tokens, management links, and passwords out of prompts and transcripts.
Use the original workspace and exact saved reader link for updates. Resolve uncertain creates before authorizing another one.
anti_patterns: Do not publish an entire workspace when only a build output is intended.
Do not treat a link-only publication as private. Anyone with the link can view it unless it is password protected.
Do not approve a changed archive with an old review digest or turn a failed update into a new publication.

faq.question: What inputs can I publish?
faq.answer: You can publish HTML, Markdown, JSON, a single file, or a static site from a directory or supported ZIP.

faq.question: Does a reader link make the content private?
faq.answer: No. Anyone with a link-only URL can view it unless a password protects it. Choose the public namespace only when you intend public listing.

faq.question: Where are owner credentials stored?
faq.answer: The runner keeps them in owner-only application state for the operating system account and resolved workspace. It reports the reader link, not the token.

faq.question: Can I update a page from another workspace?
faq.answer: Use the original workspace, the same operating system account, and the exact saved reader URL. This edition does not search other workspaces for proof.

faq.question: Does archive confirmation prove there are no secrets?
faq.answer: No. It binds approval to an archive digest. Encoded values, unsupported formats, and unreviewed metadata still need independent review.

faq.question: What should I do if a create has an unknown outcome?
faq.answer: Check the pending operation and recover a protected receipt if available. Otherwise verify the outcome through BrewPage before recording it or authorizing another create.
